BankingAbroad.title: Banking abroad
BankingAbroad.description: Opening a bank account in your study country: what banks usually ask for, which accounts are open to international students, and how credit history works there. All from official and bank sources.
BankingAbroad.aboutYouHint: Bank eligibility depends on more than nationality: visa, residency, age and student status all matter.
BankingAbroad.askFirst: Before CaiMao can say which banks are likely to accept you, it needs your {fields}.
BankingAbroad.howTitle: How to open a bank account in {country}

1.title: Check eligibility
1.body: Banks look at your immigration status, residency, age and whether you're a student. These are the factors on record:

2.title: Prepare your documents
2.body: Gather originals before you apply. Typical documents:

3.title: Choose an account type
3.body: Student and newcomer accounts often have lower fees. Compare monthly fees, minimum balances and international transfer support below.

4.title: Choose a bank
4.body: Pick an account you're likely to be eligible for, then check the bank's own page for the latest requirements.

5.title: Apply online or in a branch
5.body: Some banks let international students apply online; others ask you to visit a branch with your originals.

6.title: Complete identity checks
6.body: The bank verifies your identity and immigration status. Answer its questions accurately; it may ask about where your money comes from.

7.title: Receive your account and card
7.body: Your account details and debit card usually arrive by post or in the app. Keep your PIN and card details private.

8.title: Set up digital banking
8.body: Install the bank's app, turn on notifications and two-factor sign-in, and add your account to CaiMao's Financial Setup.

BankingAbroad.banksHint: Taken from each bank's own website. Anything the bank's page didn't confirm is marked "Not confirmed".
BankingAbroad.bankDecides: Only the bank can decide whether to open an account for you. Requirements can vary by branch and by customer, so treat this as guidance and confirm with the bank.
BankingAbroad.planBody: CaiMao turns this into a step-by-step plan: documents, bank account, transfers from home, tuition, recurring payments and credit history.

Agent.help: I can work through a payment end to end: find what's due, check your balances and the transfer rules, compare providers on what actually arrives, and prepare the transfer for your approval. I can also analyse a bank statement, check cross-border rules for any of my five countries, help you open a bank account abroad, explain local credit history and switch languages.

Your payment is due in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Paying on time helps maintain a positive payment history. Paying the full statement balance, rather than the {minimum} minimum, also avoids interest.
